## References

The articles on Time Series Made Simple draw on the resources below. Direct quotes
and code examples are credited within each article, and especially helpful links
are included there as well.

**Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). *Forecasting: Principles and practice*
(3rd ed.). OTexts. <https://otexts.com/fpp3>**

Probably the most widely used text on forecasting and time series: well organized,
accessible, and free online. Its examples are in R while this site uses Python, but
the principles carry over, and most methods have direct equivalents in libraries
like statsmodels.

**Nielsen, A. (2019). *Practical time series analysis: Prediction with statistics and
machine learning*. O'Reilly Media.**

A useful companion text, a little less structured than Hyndman, with examples in
both Python and R.

**McKinney, W. (2022). *Python for data analysis: Data wrangling with pandas, NumPy,
and Jupyter* (3rd ed.). O'Reilly Media.**

The standard guide to pandas, including a full chapter on time series data.

**Documentation**

- [statsmodels](https://www.statsmodels.org)
- [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org)

## How AI Is Used

Every article is drafted by me. I use AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to
proofread, flag possible technical errors, and brainstorm structure. I also use AI to make coding suggestions but not to draw up large code blocks. I review and verify every suggestion myself, and all code is run and tested before it's published. AI does not write the articles.
